spots.name: Toledo Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Primatial Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Toledo, Spain. It is the seat of the Metropolitan Archdiocese of Toledo. Since 1088, it holds the honorific title of Primatial, granted by Urban II, establishing a higher rank over the rest in the Iberian Peninsula.

spots.name: Monastery of San Juan de los Reyes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Monastery of San Juan de los Reyes is an Isabelline style Franciscan monastery in Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain, built by the Catholic Monarchs (1477–1504).
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monastery of San Juan de los Reyes

spots.name: Alcázar of Toledo

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Alcázar of Toledo is a stone fortification located in the highest part of Toledo, Spain. It is a large quadrangular building measuring 60 meters on a side, framed by four large towers 60 meters high, each crowned by the typical Madrid spire.

spots.name: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca
spots.summary: The Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca, also known as the Ibn Shoshan Synagogue, is a former Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 4 Calle Reyes Católicos, in the historic old city of Toledo, in the province of Castilla-La Mancha, Spain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca

spots.name: Church of Cristo de la Luz
spots.summary: The Church of Cristo de la Luz is a Catholic chapel and former mosque located in Toledo, Spain. It is one of the ten mosques that existed in the city during the period of Muslim rule. Originally known as the Mezquita Bab al-Mardum, its name was derived from the nearby city gate, Bab al-Mardum.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Cristo de la Luz

spots.name: Plaza de Zocodover, Toledo
spots.summary: The Plaza de Zocodover is a square in the city of Toledo, in the autonomous community of Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It was the central hub of the city during most of its history, acting as its main square. Part of it was designed by Juan de Herrera during the reign of Philip II.

spots.name: Puente de San Martín
spots.summary: The Puente de San Martín is a medieval bridge across the river Tagus in Toledo, Spain.

spots.name: El Greco Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The El Greco Museum is a single-artist museum in Toledo, Spain, devoted to the work and life of El Greco, who spent much of his life in Toledo, having been born in Fodele, Crete. It is one of the National Museums of Spain and it is attached to the Ministry of Culture.

spots.name: Puy du Fou España
spots.summary: Puy du Fou España is a Spanish historical theme park opened in 2021 and located in the outskirts of Toledo, in the autonomous community of Castile-La Mancha. The park is part of the French group Association du Puy du Fou. The shows are based on the history of Spain.

spots.name: Synagogue of El Tránsito

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Synagogue of El Tránsito, also known as the Synagogue of Samuel ha-Levi or Halevi, is a former Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at on Calle Samuel Levi, in the historic old city of Toledo, in the province of Castilla-La Mancha, Spain.

spots.name: Church of Santo Tomé
spots.summary: The Iglesia de Santo Tomé is a church located in the historical center of the city of Toledo (Spain), and was founded after the reconquest of this city by King Alfonso VI of León. It appears quoted in the 12th century, as constructed on the site of an old mosque of the 11th century.

spots.name: Castle of San Servando

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Castle of San Servando is a medieval castle in Toledo, Spain, near the Tagus River. It was begun as a monastery, occupied first by monks and later by the Knights Templar.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Puerta de Bisagra Nueva
spots.summary: The Puerta de Bisagra Nueva is the best known city gate of Toledo, Spain.

spots.name: Puente de Alcántara

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Puente de Alcántara is a Roman arch bridge in Toledo, Spain, spanning the River Tagus. The word Alcántara comes from Arabic القنطرة (al-qanṭarah), which means "arch".

spots.name: Museum of Santa Cruz

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Santa Cruz is an art, archaeology and ethnographic museum located in the historic centre of the city of Toledo, Spain. It exhibits collections pertaining to the province of Toledo, including works painted by El Greco in the city of Toledo.

spots.name: Church of Santiago, Toledo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St James the Great, known in Spanish as Iglesia de Santiago el Mayor or de Santiago del Arrabal, is a 13th-century Roman Catholic church in Toledo, Spain.

spots.name: Puerta del Sol
spots.summary: Puerta del Sol is a city gate of Toledo, Spain, built by the Knights Hospitaller between the late 13th and early 14th centuries. The gate is a notable example of Mudéjar military architecture, combining Romanesque and Islamic elements.

spots.name: Church of San Ildefonso, Toledo
spots.summary: The Church of San Ildefonso is a Baroque style church located in the historic center of the city of Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It is also known as the Jesuit church and is consecrated to Saint Ildefonso of Toledo, patron of the city and Father of the Church.

spots.name: Jewish quarter of Toledo
spots.summary: The Jewish quarter of Toledo is a district of the city of Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It was the neighborhood in which Jews were known to live in during the Middle Ages, though they were not mandated to live in it.

spots.name: Capilla de los Reyes Nuevos (Catedral de Toledo)

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Toledo railway station
spots.summary: The Toledo railway station is a railway station in Toledo, Spain, which was designed by architect Narciso Clavería y de Palacios in the Neo-Mudéjar style.

spots.name: Church of San Román

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Iglesia de San Román is a church in Toledo. The church was built in the Mudéjar style in the 13th century. On this site there was an old Visigothic structure and probably an ancient Roman building.

spots.name: Puerta de Bisagra
spots.summary: The Puerta de Bisagra is a city gate of Toledo, Spain.

spots.name: Monastery of Saint Dominic of Silos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Monastery of Saint Dominic of Silos (the Old) (Spanish: Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Silos (el Antiguo)) is a Cistercian convent in Toledo, Spain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monastery of Saint Dominic of Silos (the Old)

spots.name: Puerta del Cambrón
spots.summary: The Puerta del Cambrón is a gate located in the west sector of the Spanish city of Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha.

spots.name: Army Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of the Army is a military museum in Toledo, Spain, devoted to the history of the Spanish Army. It is one of the National Museums of Spain and it is attached to the Ministry of Defence.

spots.name: Church of Santa Leocadia, Toledo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Leocadia is a medieval church located in Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Mosque of las Tornerías

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mosque of las Tornerías is a former mosque in Toledo, in the Castile-La Mancha of Spain. The former Moorish-style mosque was built in the middle of the 11th century on the foundations of Roman architecture, located in the old Muslim neighborhood Arrabal de Francos.

spots.name: Archbishop's Palace of Toledo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio Arzobispal de Toledo or Archbishop's Palace of Toledo is a palace located in front of the Cathedral and next to the City Hall in the city of Toledo, region of Castile-La Mancha, Spain.

photo.author: Turol Jones, un artista de cojones from Villanueva del Cascajal, República Indep

spots.name: Cave of Hercules
spots.summary: The Cave of Hercules is a subterranean vaulted space dating back to Roman times located in the alley of San Ginés in the city of Toledo, Spain. The cave is under a building located where the Church of San Ginés, Toledo stood until 1841.

spots.name: Church of El Salvador
spots.summary: The Iglesia de El Salvador is a church in Toledo, Spain completed in 1159.

spots.name: Palacio de Galiana

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio de Galiana is a Mudéjar palace in Toledo, Spain, on the borders of the Tagus River. It was built on the site of an earlier summer villa and garden of Al-Mamun, the king of the Taifa of Toledo, in the thirteenth century by king Alfonso X of Castile.

spots.name: Hospital de Tavera
spots.summary: The Hospital de Tavera, also known as the Hospital de San Juan Bautista, Hospital de afuera, or simply as Hospital Tavera, is an important building of Renaissance architecture located in the Spanish city of Toledo. It was built between 1541 and 1603 by order of the Cardinal Tavera.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Puerta de Alcántara
spots.summary: The Alcantara Gate is a city gate located in Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It gives access to the interior of the historic center of the city, passing through its eastern side the surrounding wall.

spots.name: Sephardic Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sephardic Museum is a museum in Toledo, Spain, devoted to the Jewish cultural heritage in Spain, as well as of the Sephardim, the descendants of the Jews who lived on the Iberian peninsula until 1492. It occupies the former convent of the Knights of Calatrava, annexed to the Synagogue of El Tránsito.

photo.author: Maxim B. from Atlanta, GA, USA

spots.name: Puerta Bab al-Mardum
spots.summary: The Puerta Bab al-Mardum, or Puerta de Valmardón, is a city-gate of Toledo, Spain. It was built in the 10th century and is one of the oldest gates in the city. Its name 'mardum' is Arabic for 'blocked up'. Perhaps because its function was taken over by the Puerta del Sol.

spots.name: Church fences of the Cathedral of Toledo
Convento de San Pedro Mártir

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Convento de San Pedro Mártir is a convent located in Toledo, Spain. The Dominican convent was moved in 1407 from its location outside the walls to the houses donated by Doña Guiomar de Meneses. Through its successive extensions and modifications, it became one of the richest and most important convents in the city.

spots.name: Convento de Santa Fé

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Convent of Santa Fe is a former monastery situated in Toledo, Spain. It is situated in the north-east of the historic centre of the city. Included in the heritage listing Bien de Interés Cultural, it has been protected since 30 September 1919.

spots.name: Real Colegio de Doncellas Nobles
spots.summary: The Colegio de Doncellas Nobles is a former girls' school in Toledo. It was founded in 1551 by the archbishop of Toledo and cardinal Juan Martínez Silíceo. The project, which had as its patron the king Philip II as well as the archbishop, had as its object the education of young women to be good mothers.

spots.name: Convento de Santa Isabel de los Reyes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Convento de Santa Isabel de los Reyes is a convent located in the city of Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Convento de Santa Isabel de los Reyes

spots.name: Palacio de La Cava

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio de los Duques de Maqueda, also known as Palacio de La Cava, is a palace located in Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain.

spots.name: Teatro Rojas
spots.summary: The Teatro Rojas is a theater in the city of Toledo, Castile-La Mancha, Spain, inaugurated in 1879 on the site of the old corral de comedias, Mesón de la Fruta. Its construction involved several architects, and it is named after the local playwright Francisco de Rojas.

spots.name: Convento de la Madre de Dios, Toledo
spots.summary: The Convento de la Madre de Dios is a Dominican convent located in the city of Toledo. It was established at the end of the 15th century as a nunnery by Leonor and María de Silva, daughters of the Count of Cifuentes.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Convento de la Madre de Dios, Toledo

spots.name: Monasterio de Santo Domingo el Real
spots.summary: The Monastery of Santo Domingo Real, located in the city of Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain, is a convent founded in 1364 by the noblewoman Inés García de Meneses, daughter of García Suárez de Meneses and María Fernández Barroso, after she was widowed by Sancho de Velasco.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monastery of Santo Domingo el Real, Toledo

spots.name: Plaza de las Cuatro Calles
spots.summary: The Plaza de las Cuatro Calles is a square located in the city of Toledo, in Castile-La Mancha, Spain. This square is the commercial heart of Toledo.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Plaza de las Cuatro Calles, Toledo

spots.name: Church of St Just and St Rufina

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Iglesia de las Santas Justa y Rufina is a medieval church in Toledo, Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It is one of a group of so-called Mozarabic parish churches in Toledo, whose existence has been documented since 1156.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Iglesia de las Santas Justa y Rufina, Toledo

spots.name: Ermita del Cristo de la Vega

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ermita del Cristo de la Vega is a hermitage located in Toledo, Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It was built on the remains of the Visigothic Basílica de Santa Leocadia during the 7th century.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Ermita del Cristo de la Vega

spots.summary: The Iglesia de San Vicente is a medieval church located in Toledo, it appears as a parish already in 1125, although, there is documentation that speaks of its being founded by Alfonso VI shortly after his conquest of the city in 1085.

spots.name: Roman circus of Toledo

spots.summary: The Roman circus of Toledo is an Ancient Roman circus site of Hispania. It served the city of Toletum, the present-day Toledo, Castilla-La Mancha, Spain.

spots.summary: The Convento de los Carmelitas Descalzos is a Discalced Carmelite convent dating to 1643 located in the city of Toledo. Azulejos panels from the 18th century covers the central nave and the chapels. The altarpieces was introduced from other buildings.

spots.summary: The Convent of the Franciscan Conceptionists is a Catholic convent of the Order of the Immaculate Conception, founded in 1484 by Saint Beatrice of Silva and located in Toledo, Spain. It is protected by the heritage listing Bien de Interés Cultural.

spots.name: Meson de la Orza
spots.summary: Great food, great service, not so cheap, but it is worthy. Dishes include; lomo de orza, pork tenderloin; migas, a traditional Spanish breadcrumb dish served with lamb sweetbreads; roast suckling lamb and pig; partridge on arroz meloso; and vanilla-infused fried milk pudding. Wine list of 100 wines.
